question.prompt:
Square \(ABCD\) has side length \(10.\) Point \(E\) is on \(\overline{BC},\) and the area of \(\triangle ABE\) is \(40.\) What is \(BE?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2013_AMC_10A_Q03_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Adjacent sides of a square are perpendicular. Since \(E\) lies on \(BC\), triangle \(ABE\) has base \(BE\) and height \(AB=10\). Its area therefore gives
\[
40=\frac12\cdot BE\cdot10=5BE.
\]
Dividing by \(5\), we obtain \(BE=8\), which lies on the side of length \(10\). The answer is \(\boxed{8}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
solutions.title: Triangle area
